# Code craft

`sde-fullstack` requires you to match the codebase's idioms. This is where they live.

**The repository outranks this file.** Every rule here is the default when the codebase has no
opinion; where the surrounding code has an established pattern, match the code and apply the
*reason* behind the rule through its conventions. A file written in the house style is worth more
than a file written in the best style.

Two rules that hold in every language:

- **The dangerous operations are the silent ones.** A crash is a good outcome; the failure modes
  worth memorizing are the ones that continue with wrong state — a swallowed exception, an unchecked
  error return, a loop that exits early with a zero status, a dry-run that dries the wrong half.
- **Read the neighbors before writing.** Two files near what you're changing tell you more about
  what will be accepted than any style guide.

## Load the reference for what you're writing

| If the work involves… | Read first |
|---|---|
| Python | [`references/python.md`](references/python.md) |
| TypeScript or JavaScript — language-level code in any framework | [`references/typescript.md`](references/typescript.md) |
| Bash or a shell script | [`references/bash.md`](references/bash.md) |
| PowerShell | [`references/powershell.md`](references/powershell.md) |
| Go | [`references/go.md`](references/go.md) |
| writing tests, or code that has none | [`references/tdd.md`](references/tdd.md) |
| changing code that already works | [`references/safe-refactor.md`](references/safe-refactor.md) |

A language not listed is not an exemption: apply the two rules above, read the neighbors, and follow
the ecosystem's own idiomatic guide (its standard formatter and linter settle style — argue with
neither).

Trips two predicates? Read both. Writing new Python with tests and touching working code trips
three, and all three apply.

The **review packet** is the end-of-task report defined by the calling agent. Invoked standalone with
no packet convention in context, end with: Changed / Assumptions / Verified / Not verified — and name
which references you read.
